text: Before a euthanasia visit, we price it, get the family's consent, and get a card on file. Then the day itself is only about the pet and the family.
Clementine's visit is in two days. Right-click it,
go to Visit Prep,
and choose Send Euthanasia Consent.
This is the estimate. Usually whoever books the visit builds it ahead of time, so it may already be here. If it's empty, here's how.
Type Euthanasia Group in the search,
and pick the package. It walks you through the choices.
Pick the euthanasia for the pet. Clementine is a cat.
Click Next.
Pick the aftercare the family wants: private cremation, with her ashes returned.
Next.
Add the same-day fee only for a same-day visit. Click Add.
Check the lines. We always price the visit first, because the consent form shows the family one total.
the weight,
and the aftercare. The form asks the family to confirm it, so make sure it matches what they asked for.
This box shows the card. Right now, there's no card on file.
Most families sign the online form. Click Email consent.
It's sent, and the link is copied, in case you want to text it yourself.
Here's what the family sees. Four short steps: their details, aftercare and the items they'd like, their consent, and the card.
If a family can't manage the form, take the card over the phone instead. Use one or the other for a visit, not both. Here's the phone path.
Right-click the visit again,
and go to Visit Prep. It now says Re-send Euthanasia Consent, because the form went out.
Open it,
and click Take card by phone.
Read the family this first: their card won't be charged until the day of the visit.
Then type the card as they read it out. In this demo, it's Stripe's test card.
Click Authorize.
Now the box turns green: card on file, and the amount held. Nothing is charged until the visit.
Close the estimate.
The visit on the schedule now shows a green dollar sign, so anyone can see the card is held.

On the form, the family reads that a hold is not a charge. You never place or move the hold yourself. Scout places it about a day before the visit, moves it if the visit moves, and releases it if the visit is cancelled.
Client liaisons: this call is usually yours. The family hears the plan, and you take the card.

Two mistakes to avoid: sending the consent before the estimate is right, and charging the family over the phone. Fix the estimate first, and remember, we only hold. Nothing is charged until the visit.
